title: Expanding Immunization Provider Access: A Policy Analysis
summary: Expands the categories of healthcare professionals authorized to administer vaccines under appropriate supervision, including registered pharmacy technicians, certified medical assistants, and nursing students, to address immunization access gaps particularly in underserved communities.
text: Educational example, not proposed legislation. This document is provided by the SAFE Research Institute for educational analysis of how a policy approach might be structured. It is not a bill, and its inclusion here is not a recommendation to adopt any measure. This educational example examines an approach relating to public health; expanding the categories of health care professionals authorized to administer vaccines; establishing supervision, training, and certification requirements; and providing for related matters. Section 1. Purpose (a) This example is premised on the following findings: 1. Timely access to immunization services is essential to protecting individual and community health, yet significant access gaps persist in rural, frontier, and medically underserved communities across the state. 2. Existing restrictions on which health care professionals may administer vaccines limit the capacity of health care delivery systems to meet patient demand, particularly during periods of heightened need such as seasonal influenza campaigns and public health emergencies. 3. Multiple categories of trained health care professionals possess the clinical competency to safely administer vaccines under appropriate supervision, yet are not currently authorized to do so under state law. 4. Expanding the categories of authorized immunization providers, with proper safeguards, will increase vaccination access, reduce wait times, and improve immunization coverage rates without compromising patient safety. (b) The purpose of this measure is to authorize additional categories of health care professionals to administer vaccines under defined supervision and training requirements, thereby expanding immunization access throughout the state. Section 2. Definitions As used in this measure: 1. "Authorized immunization provider" means any individual authorized under this measure or other provisions of state law to administer vaccines. 2. "Certified medical assistant" means an individual who holds a current certification from a nationally recognized medical assistant credentialing organization and is employed by or under contract with a licensed health care facility or practitioner. 3. "Direct supervision" means that a supervising practitioner is present in the same facility and immediately available to provide assistance and direction during the administration of a vaccine. 4. "Nursing student" means an individual enrolled in an accredited registered nursing or practical nursing program who has completed coursework in pharmacology and injection technique. 5. "Registered pharmacy technician" means an individual registered as a pharmacy technician with the state board of pharmacy who is in good standing. 6. "Supervising practitioner" means a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, physician assistant, or pharmacist licensed in this state. Section 3. Authorized Immunization Providers (a) In addition to those health care professionals currently authorized to administer vaccines under state law, the following individuals may administer vaccines in accordance with this measure: 1. Registered pharmacy technicians, under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist; 2. Certified medical assistants, under the direct supervision of a licensed physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant; 3. Nursing students who have completed the training requirements of Section 5 of this measure, under the direct supervision of a licensed registered nurse, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician; 4. Emergency medical technicians certified at the basic level or above, under the direct supervision of a physician or pursuant to standing orders issued by a physician medical director. (b) An authorized immunization provider under this section may administer any vaccine included on the immunization schedule published by the state department of health, subject to the supervision and training requirements of this measure. Section 4. Supervision Requirements (a) No individual authorized solely under this measure shall administer a vaccine unless a supervising practitioner is present in the same facility and immediately available. (b) A supervising practitioner may supervise no more than four authorized immunization providers simultaneously. (c) The supervising practitioner shall review and co-sign all immunization records completed by an authorized immunization provider under this measure within twenty-four hours of vaccine administration. (d) The supervising practitioner shall be responsible for ensuring that all pre-screening assessments, including review of contraindications and patient history, are completed prior to vaccine administration. Section 5. Training and Certification (a) Prior to administering vaccines under this measure, each authorized immunization provider shall complete a training program that includes, at minimum: 1. Not fewer than four hours of didactic instruction covering vaccine storage and handling, immunization schedules, contraindications, proper injection technique, and infection control procedures; 2. A hands-on clinical practicum including the administration of not fewer than five injections under direct observation by a supervising practitioner; 3. Current certification in cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and basic first aid; 4. Training in the recognition and emergency management of anaphylaxis and other adverse reactions, including the use of epinephrine auto-injectors. (b) Training programs under this section shall be approved by the state department of health and may be offered by accredited educational institutions, health care facilities, professional associations, or the department itself. (c) Each authorized immunization provider shall complete not fewer than two hours of continuing education in immunization practice annually to maintain authorization under this measure. Section 6. Liability Protections (a) An authorized immunization provider who administers a vaccine in compliance with this measure and within the scope of their authorization shall be entitled to the same liability protections available under federal and state law to other health care professionals who administer vaccines. (b) A supervising practitioner shall not incur additional liability solely by reason of supervising an authorized immunization provider under this measure, provided that the supervising practitioner has fulfilled the supervision and oversight obligations set forth in Section 4. (c) Nothing in this measure shall be construed to limit or alter the protections afforded under the National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act of 1986 or the Public Readiness and Emergency Preparedness Act. Section 7. Reporting Requirements (a) Each authorized immunization provider shall report all vaccines administered to the state immunization information system within twenty-four hours of administration, in accordance with existing state reporting requirements. (b) The state department of health shall publish an annual report summarizing the number of vaccines administered by authorized immunization providers under this measure, including data disaggregated by provider category, geographic region, and patient demographics. (c) Any adverse event following immunization administered by an authorized immunization provider under this measure shall be reported in accordance with existing state and federal adverse event reporting requirements, including submission to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS). Section 8. Effective Date This measure shall take effect one hundred eighty days after enactment, provided that the state department of health shall promulgate regulations necessary for implementation within one hundred twenty days of enactment. Policy Considerations This model legislation represents one approach to expanding the immunization workforce through broadened scope of practice. Legislators considering this template should evaluate: - Scope of practice boundaries and the positions of state medical boards, nursing boards, and pharmacy boards regarding delegation of vaccine administration to additional provider categories - Whether the specified supervision ratios and training requirements are sufficient to maintain patient safety, particularly for pediatric populations and individuals with complex medical histories - Liability and malpractice insurance implications for newly authorized provider categories and their supervising practitioners - Fiscal impact on state budgets and healthcare systems - Compatibility with existing state statutes and regulatory frameworks The SAFE Research Institute presents this material as an educational resource and does not advocate for or against any specific legislative outcome. --- This document is provided by the SAFE Research Institute as an educational resource. It is not legal advice. It is offered to inform analysis and discussion, not to promote the adoption of any particular measure. Readers should consult qualified professionals regarding their existing health professional licensing frameworks, constitutional provisions, and administrative procedures.

title: Evidence-Based Immunization Guidance: A Policy Analysis
summary: Authorizes state health departments to establish immunization recommendations based on guidance from recognized medical professional organizations, creating a framework for state-level immunization scheduling independent of federal advisory processes.
text: Educational example, not proposed legislation. This document is provided by the SAFE Research Institute for educational analysis of how a policy approach might be structured. It is not a bill, and its inclusion here is not a recommendation to adopt any measure. This educational example examines an approach relating to public health; authorizing the state department of health to establish immunization recommendations based on guidance from recognized medical professional organizations; and providing for related matters. Section 1. Purpose and Findings (a) This example is premised on the following findings: 1. Immunization is among the most effective public health interventions in history, preventing millions of cases of disease, disability, and death each year. 2. The health and welfare of the residents of this state depend upon timely access to immunizations guided by the best available scientific and clinical evidence. 3. Recognized medical professional organizations, through rigorous peer-reviewed processes, develop and maintain immunization recommendations grounded in current epidemiological data, clinical trial evidence, and established principles of preventive medicine. 4. It is in the interest of the state to ensure that its immunization recommendations remain aligned with the prevailing scientific consensus, even in the event of disruption, delay, or alteration of federal advisory processes. (b) The purpose of this measure is to authorize the state department of health to promulgate immunization schedules and recommendations informed by the guidance of recognized medical professional organizations, thereby safeguarding continuity of evidence-based immunization practice within the state. Section 2. Definitions As used in this measure: 1. "Department" means the state department of health or its successor agency. 2. "Director" means the director of the department or the director's designee. 3. "Immunization recommendation" means a clinical guideline specifying the vaccines, dosing schedules, age-appropriate timing, and target populations for immunization within the state. 4. "Recognized medical professional organization" means an organization designated under Section 4 of this measure. 5. "State Immunization Advisory Committee" means the committee established under Section 3 of this measure. Section 3. State Immunization Advisory Authority (a) There is hereby established within the department a State Immunization Advisory Committee, composed of not fewer than nine members appointed by the director, including: 1. At least three physicians licensed in the state with expertise in infectious disease, pediatrics, or preventive medicine; 2. At least one representative from the state's public health laboratory system; 3. At least one immunologist or vaccinologist affiliated with an accredited research institution; 4. At least one representative of a federally qualified health center operating within the state; 5. At least two public members, one of whom shall have expertise in health equity. (b) The committee shall convene no fewer than four times per calendar year and shall advise the director on the adoption, modification, or withdrawal of immunization recommendations. (c) The director, upon consultation with the committee, shall have the authority to issue, amend, or rescind immunization recommendations applicable within the state. Section 4. Recognized Medical Professional Organizations (a) For purposes of this measure, the following organizations are designated as recognized medical professional organizations: 1. The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP); 2. The American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP); 3. The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG); 4. The American College of Physicians (ACP); 5. The American Medical Association (AMA). (b) The director may, by regulation and upon recommendation of the committee, designate additional organizations as recognized medical professional organizations provided that such organizations maintain transparent, peer-reviewed processes for developing clinical immunization guidance. Section 5. Baseline Recommendations (a) The department shall maintain a baseline immunization schedule that, at minimum, incorporates the most recent immunization recommendations published by any two or more of the recognized medical professional organizations listed in Section 4. (b) In the event that federal immunization recommendations are suspended, materially delayed, or diverge from the prevailing consensus of the recognized medical professional organizations, the department shall issue interim guidance consistent with the consensus of such organizations. (c) Nothing in this measure shall be construed to prohibit the department from adopting recommendations that exceed federal recommendations where supported by the scientific evidence reviewed by the committee. Section 6. Periodic Review (a) The committee shall conduct a comprehensive review of the state immunization schedule not less than once per calendar year, taking into account: 1. Updated guidance from the recognized medical professional organizations; 2. Current epidemiological surveillance data from within the state and nationally; 3. Emerging evidence from peer-reviewed scientific literature; 4. Immunization coverage rates and disparities among populations within the state. (b) Following each review, the committee shall publish a written report summarizing its findings and any recommended changes to the state immunization schedule. Such report shall be made publicly available on the department's website. Section 7. Severability If any provision of this measure, or its application to any person or circumstance, is held invalid, the invalidity does not affect other provisions or applications of this measure that can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of this measure are severable. Policy Considerations This model legislation represents one approach to establishing state-level immunization scheduling authority. Legislators considering this template should evaluate: - The potential for divergence between state and federal immunization recommendations, and the resulting complexity for healthcare providers, insurers, and patients navigating different schedules - Whether the designated medical professional organizations adequately represent the range of clinical perspectives, and the process for adding or removing organizations from the list - Administrative costs and expertise required to staff and sustain a State Immunization Advisory Committee with the technical capacity to independently evaluate vaccine evidence - Fiscal impact on state budgets and healthcare systems - Compatibility with existing state statutes and regulatory frameworks The SAFE Research Institute presents this material as an educational resource and does not advocate for or against any specific legislative outcome. --- This document is provided by the SAFE Research Institute as an educational resource.
